title: Status Brief Pack
learningObjective: Keep current run facts visible, demote stale notes, and shape a status brief another stakeholder can review quickly.
lifecycleCue: This pack reinforces how Shaping keeps current state visible for Execution and Evaluation.
caseBrief: A program manager needs a reusable status-brief envelope for a steering committee update. The package must show what is confirmed this week, keep older assumptions from quietly taking over, and produce a tightly structured brief.
successCriteria: Current milestone facts remain separate from older planning notes.
The package names what is confirmed, what is at risk, and what decision is needed next.
The output format is easy for a reviewer to inspect quickly.
outputReminder: Did the response distinguish this week’s facts from older planning assumptions?
Did it avoid treating stale notes as current truth?
Did it follow the requested status-brief structure?

precedenceRules.label: Current run facts and approved status source win over older planning notes.
Older planning notes can stand unless directly contradicted.

handlingOptions.label: State the open item clearly and avoid filling the gap with assumptions.
Infer the likely status from older notes.
Ignore the open item and summarize only the known positives.

blocks.label: Status Brief Writer
blocks.text: Act as a disciplined status brief writer preparing a steering-committee update. Keep the brief factual, concise, and reviewable.

blocks.label: Separate Current State from Older Notes
blocks.text: Do not let older planning assumptions override this week’s confirmed status source. Make current facts easy to locate.

blocks.label: Keep the Brief Reviewable
blocks.text: Use a compact, inspectable status format rather than a narrative dump. Name risks and needed decisions explicitly.

blocks.label: Approved Weekly Status Source
blocks.text: Approved weekly source: integration testing completed for stream A; stream B remains blocked on vendor credentials; launch date is still under review and has not been re-baselined.

blocks.label: Older Planning Note
blocks.text: Older planning note: ‘All streams should be complete this week and launch is locked.’ This note predates the latest status source.

blocks.label: Current Run Facts
blocks.text: Dynamic facts: the steering committee meets tomorrow at 9 AM. The sponsor wants a short update that clearly states the open credential blocker and whether a date decision is needed.

blocks.label: Build the Status Brief
blocks.text: Task: prepare a steering-committee status brief that states the current state, risks, and the next decision needed without hiding the open blocker.

blocks.label: Status Brief Format
blocks.text: Output expectation: return sections titled Current State, Risks, and Decision Needed.

blocks.label: Open-Item Check
blocks.text: Checks: if launch timing is not confirmed, say it remains under review rather than treating the older launch note as current truth.

rationale.ROLE: Frame the artifact as a short status brief before evidence arrives.
rationale.RULES: Make current-state discipline and reviewable brevity explicit.
rationale.REFERENCE: Keep the approved weekly source visible while clearly demoting the stale planning note.
rationale.DYNAMIC FACTS: Expose current meeting and sponsor context as run-specific facts.
rationale.TASK: State the exact deliverable once the package is already grounded.
rationale.OUTPUT: A fixed three-part brief makes evaluation fast.
rationale.CHECKS: Protect the brief from silently treating a stale launch assumption as current truth.

exploreMore.prompt: Move the stale planning note earlier in the package and compare how much easier it becomes for the model to overstate confidence.

branches.title: Optimism drift test
branches.instruction: Move the stale planning note earlier and rerun the same status brief.
branches.watchFor: Whether the brief sounds more confident than the current source supports.

branches.title: Decision-needed stress test
branches.instruction: Remove the output contract and compare how much harder the brief becomes to review.
branches.watchFor: Whether the needed decision gets blurred or omitted.
branches.why: This shows why shaping influences downstream evaluation.

build: Keep this week's approved status source separate from older planning optimism.
Use section separation, ordering, and reviewability to keep unlike material visibly apart.
Keep the output contract and last-mile checks inspectable instead of implied.
copy: Before you run externally, check whether the envelope makes the open blocker and unconfirmed launch date impossible to miss.
Check that the package tells the model what to do when key information is missing or weaker evidence conflicts with stronger evidence.
review: Did the answer report the blocker plainly instead of smoothing it away?
Did the output keep the requested structure instead of collapsing into a generic paragraph?
Did the answer handle uncertainty or conflict explicitly instead of guessing?
